companyDescription: AI Data Center Networking · High-speed connectivity silicon (AEC cables, SerDes, line card chips) enabling hyperscaler AI clusters — the bandwidth backbone of AI infrastructure
priceNote: $238.90, down ~14% from Jul 6's $276 as guidance-disappointment overhang + broader semi pullback + CFO/CTO routine 10b5-1 selling weighed on shares. Still well below Stifel $350 / BofA $340 targets. Q1 FY27 earnings Sep 9 — guided $465-475M revenue.
summary: Credo has pulled back ~14% since its Q4 FY26 beat (Jun 1) to $238.90, driven by a guidance-disappointment overhang and pre-arranged CFO/CTO 10b5-1 stock sales rather than any change in the underlying thesis. Q4 FY26 revenue hit $437M (+157% YoY), guiding Q1 FY27 to $465-475M, and analyst targets (Stifel $350, BofA/Evercore $340) are unchanged. The AI networking AEC/optical demand cycle remains structurally intact; the pullback looks like sentiment/technical, not fundamental, with Sep 9 earnings the next real test.

catalysts.name: Hyperscaler AI Fabric Expansion
catalysts.description: Microsoft, Google, Amazon are building 100GbE+ AI cluster interconnects — Credo's Active Electrical Cables (AEC) and line card chips are the key enabling technology. AI capex cycle drives sticky multi-year revenue.

catalysts.name: Q1 FY27 Earnings
catalysts.description: Sep 9, 2026. Guided revenue $465-475M (+6-9% QoQ). Street watches whether 157% YoY growth continues and whether the post-beat pullback reverses on a fresh beat-and-raise.

catalysts.name: Post-Selloff Stabilization Watch
catalysts.description: Stock down ~14% since Jun 1 high on guidance overhang + CFO/CTO 10b5-1 selling (pre-arranged, not opportunistic). Analyst targets unchanged (Stifel $350, BofA/Evercore $340) — a hold above the $215-225 support zone would confirm this is sentiment, not thesis break.

risks: Customer concentration risk — single hyperscaler (believed Microsoft) represents large portion of revenue; any contract pause = revenue cliff
Competition from Marvell Technology (MRVL) and Broadcom (AVGO) in AI networking silicon
~90x P/E valuation — priced for perfection; any slowdown in hyperscaler AI capex triggers sharp derating
CFO and CTO both sold shares in July under 10b5-1 plans (pre-arranged, not opportunistic, large remaining stakes) — benign but adds to sentiment overhang during a technical pullback

estimateDates.note: Guide $465-475M rev — next beat-and-raise test, also the catalyst that resolves whether the Jul pullback was sentiment or thesis

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed hawkish tilt pressures high-P/E semis; CRDO ~90x P/E is rate-sensitive despite structural AI demand.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Semiconductor components face some cost inflation but CRDO's custom silicon pricing power absorbs this
macroRisk.sectorImpact: AI networking demand is structural and multi-year — independent of Fed rate decisions. Hyperscaler AI capex is the dominant driver.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — AI networking demand is structural, but CRDO's premium multiple makes it vulnerable to hawkish macro surprises and broader semi-sector rotation, which is the more likely explanation for the recent pullback than any thesis change.

stopLoss.tightNote: Below Jul pullback low / support test
stopLoss.hardNote: Bear case — hyperscaler pause / thesis break
stopLoss.rrWarning: Good R/R — thesis intact, pullback reads as sentiment not fundamentals

entryStrategy.verdict: Post-beat pullback (-14% since Jun 1) on guidance overhang + routine insider selling — not a thesis break. Add on further dips toward $215-225; Sep 9 earnings is the next binary. Avoid chasing above $260 without a new catalyst.

catalystSpot.preRunup: CRDO has historically run hard into earnings prints as hyperscaler AI capex checks come in strong, then consolidates or pulls back post-print even on a beat if guidance doesn't clear the bar.
catalystSpot.preRunupTiming: 2-3 สัปดาห์ก่อน earnings print

postWin.note: CRDO Q3 FY26 beat (Feb 2026) drove +22% single session on 157% revenue growth surprise. Q4 FY26 (Jun 1) gained only +1.3% day-of, then reversed into a 14% pullback by mid-Jul on guidance-disappointment overhang despite the headline beat.

postLose.note: CRDO Q1 FY26 softer guidance (Aug 2025) dropped -18% as customer ramp timing uncertainty. Any hyperscaler pause in AI capex = severe de-rating at this multiple.

spotSizing.reason: Core Holding — high conviction on AI networking structural demand, but the fresh pullback + no new catalyst until Sep 9 argues for a slightly smaller near-term size than prior runs. Max 7% of portfolio.
